readings: pedge is asserted in the same clock cycle in which in first becomes 1 (combinational edge detect using a registered previous value)
pedge is asserted one clock cycle later (pedge itself is registered, giving two-cycle latency from the 0 sample)
The previous-value register initializes to 0 (or is treated as 0), so in=1 on the first clock cycle can produce pedge=1 as if a 0->1 transition occurred
No transition can be detected before two clock cycles, so pedge must be 0 (or undefined) on the first cycle regardless of in
pedge is a one-cycle pulse, high only in the cycle immediately following the detected 0->1 transition and deasserts even if in remains 1
pedge is set to 1 and remains 1 while in stays 1 (or until a 0 is observed), acting as a level flag
